keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Mthethwa row). The only extent on the pages is Etherington's: 'dominated the areas from the Umkhomazi River which is in the south of the' Hluhluwe in the north, with the coastal lowlands exploited through the Delagoa Bay trade. The Mthethwa page itself says it 'arose in the 18th century south of Delagoa Bay' and names no river. No area figure on either page. Confidence 1: one scholar's two place names, and the page elsewhere describes a 'confederation of roughly 30 Nguni chiefdoms' with no fixed frontier.

notes: Cliopatria has no Mthethwa row; the sibling zululand dossier names mtetwa-paramountcy as predecessor with 'extent unknown', so this slug is kept. Three pages: Mthethwa_Paramountcy (thin: infobox c. 1780-1817, no area, no capital, no rivers), Dingiswayo (the only extent: Umkhomazi to Hluhluwe, Etherington 2005; reign 1806-1817 in the infobox but also c. 1800-1818 and a 'late 1810' death in the text), Ndwandwe (1817/1818 Mbuzi Hill). The box bounds 30.2S and 28.0S are the researcher's own knowledge of Umkhomazi and Hluhluwe (neither is in the gazetteer); the box is clipped to KwaZulu-Natal. It overlaps the Ndwandwe box and the sibling Zulu core of 1816 by design of the sources (Hluhluwe lies north of the Black Umfolozi, inside the Ndwandwe range). The 1811 joining of the Zulu and Buthelezi clans (Mthethwa page: 'About 1811, the Buthelezi and other Nguni groups, including the then still marginal Zulu clan led by Senzangakona, joined a confederacy dominated by the Mthethwa') is not a ledger event because the page names no land. Gazetteer names needed: Umkhomazi (river), Hluhluwe (place), Oyengweni.
